questions.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨{e}^{3t},\,{t}^{3}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨3{e}^{3t},\,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨3{t}^{3},\,-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=3.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨9{t}^{2},\,-t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=3,$ we substitute $t=3$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(3) & =⟨9(3)^{2},\,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨9\cdot 9,\,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨81,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds, is given by

$$
v=⟨6t+1,-3{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨6,-6(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨-6,6⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+({6}^{2})} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot 36} \\  & =6\sqrt{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-2{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2}-2,\,4{t}^{3}-4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6t,\,12{t}^{2}-4⟩\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{1/2}+8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-8t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{-1/2}+8,\,6t-8⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨3(1)^{-1/2}+8,\,6(1)-8⟩ \\  & =⟨3+8,\,6-8⟩ \\  & =⟨11,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}

$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =⟨30(2)-4,\,12(2)^{2}-6⟩ \\  & =⟨60-4,\,48-6⟩ \\  & =⟨56,\,42⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(2)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(2)| & =|⟨56,\,42⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{56}^{2}+{42}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3136+1764} \\  & =\sqrt{4900} \\  & =70\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the acceleration at time $t=2\,\text{s}$ is $70{\text{ m/s}}^{2}.$

questions.problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{4}{1+t},\,\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-4t+5⟩.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{1+t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-4t+5)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{(1+t)^{2}},\,{t}^{2}-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{4}{(1+t)^{2}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-4)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{8}{(1+t)^{3}},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨\frac{8}{(1+(1))^{3}},\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{8}{{2}^{3}},\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨1,\,2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
